📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Florida Rep. Darren Soto, here at a hearing in July, has won a sixth term representing the 9th District. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

Florida Rep. Darren Soto, the most vulnerable House Democrat running for reelection, narrowly won a sixth term Tuesday in a district that state Republicans redrew in their favor.

Soto was leading Republican Navy veteran Dan Green by less than a point when The Associated Press called the race for Central Florida’s 9th District a week after Election Day. His margin of victory was above the 0.5 percent threshold that would trigger a recount under state law.

House Democrats have so far flipped more than 40 seats and appear on track to hold their biggest majority in the chamber in decades. Soto’s win means that no House Democratic incumbent lost to a Republican in the general election this year. And Florida Democrats defended all four seats the GOP had hoped to pick up under the state’s upcoming Republican-drawn map.

Democratic Reps. Kathy Castor and Jared Moskowitz both won reelection from districts that shifted red, while Democrat Pia Dandiya, a former high school principal, defeated Republican Marine Corps veteran Casey Askar for a redrawn open seat in South Florida.

Soto, who declared victory last week, had been seen as the most vulnerable of the targeted Florida Democrats. The new map reduced the Hispanic population of his district as the seat shifted from one that Kamala Harris would have carried in 2024 to one that Donald Trump would have taken by 18 points.

“Despite the Florida Republican legislature’s efforts to redraw me out of this district, my record of delivering for Florida highlighted voters that I am a reliable fighter for them in Congress,” Soto mentioned in a Nov. 4 statement.

In a Tuesday memo detailing how House Democrats secured their historic majority, the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee took aim at Republicans’ mid-decade redistricting efforts, saying their “attempts to steal seats … supremely backfired.”.

It has been revealed that while Florida Republicans were unsuccessful in flipping the four Democrat-held seats, the party held all of its House seats in the Sunshine State. Republican Rep. María Elvira Salazar narrowly won reelection in the Miami-area 27th District over Democratic challenger Eliott Rodriguez, the AP reported Tuesday. In the 7th District outside Orlando, Republican former TV news anchor Ryan Elijah defeated Democratic Navy veteran Bale Dalton, a former NASA chief of staff who conceded Tuesday.

Industry News: U.S. demand for menopause hormone therapy has more than doubled recently

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Monthly dispensing of hormone therapy for women aged 40 to 74 more than doubled since 2023, growing from 2 million to 4.9 million, researchers report November 19 in JAMA.
  • Although the data in the upcoming study are aggregate, the researchers used population data to estimate the dispensing rate for this age group, which jumped from 28 prescriptions per 1,000 women to 67 prescriptions per 1,000 over the period studied.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that more U.S. women are taking menopause hormone therapy, upcoming prescription data suggest.

Monthly dispensing of hormone therapy for women aged 40 to 74 more than doubled since 2023, growing from 2 million to 4.9 million, researchers report November 19 in JAMA. The analysis of U.S. pharmacy dispensing data revealed that this increase began in 2024. The rise continued in 2025, before and after the Food and Drug Administration’s November removal of the black box warning from packaging, and into 2026.

Although the data in the upcoming study are aggregate, the researchers used population data to estimate the dispensing rate for this age group, which jumped from 28 prescriptions per 1,000 women to 67 prescriptions per 1,000 over the period studied.

In a recent development, the new study wasn’t designed to determine what’s behind the increase. It’s possible that the evidence regarding hormone therapy’s safety and effectiveness for the treatment of menopause symptoms, such as hot flashes, is reaching more women. Medical groups such as the Menopause Society have recommended menopause hormone therapy for women with symptoms who are younger than 60 or within 10 years of the start of menopause, absent certain risk factors including prior breast cancer and stroke.

“Greater attention to women’s health, updated medical guidance supporting individualized menopause hormone therapy and social media may all be contributing to increased interest,” notes Dana Sarnak, who studies sexual and reproductive health at Johns Hopkins School of Medicine. Anecdotally, her clinician colleagues report more patients seeking menopause care, she says.

In a recent development, many women and physicians turned away from hormone therapy in the early 2000s after a large study called the Women’s Health Initiative raised safety concerns, which were later considered overblown. Research since then has provided a more nuanced understanding of the benefits and risks of menopause hormone therapy at different ages.

There are safer formulations, including patches and gels, of estrogen today then at the time of the Women’s Health Initiative, for which participants took a pill. The new study found that product use increased for transdermal and vaginal estrogen and for progesterone products — women who have their uterus need to take progesterone along with estrogen. The use of oral formulations remained stable. There has been a shortage of estrogen patches in the United States this year, which the U.S. Food and Drug Administration attributes to increasing demand.

The BepiColombo spacecraft is finally entering orbit around Mercury

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., leaves a meeting in the Capitol on Tuesday, before his election as incoming minority leader later in the day. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

Senate Majority Leader John Thune was reelected as the Republican leader on Tuesday and will steer the conference through their time in the minority.

The South Dakotan ran uncontested despite a push from some of his colleagues to delay the leadership elections following Republicans’ stunning defeats last week in the midterms, which saw them lose at least seven seats and the majority.

Sources indicate that “Obviously, the election result was not what we hoped for,” Thune told reporters, referring to the midterms. “But I think it’s crucial that we take the lessons from that and internalize the message the American people were sending to us.”.

While he and the rest of the leadership slate sailed through the conference contests by voice vote, it wasn’t without drama.

According to recent reports, before the leadership elections began in the Old Supreme Court Chamber early Tuesday morning, the conference held a meeting at the request of a group of GOP five senators, led by Sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis.

According to recent reports, the conversation, which several senators described as “frank,” ended up pushing back the leadership elections by a few hours. But they were not postponed to another day as some had hoped.

“This has never been anything against John Thune,” remarked Johnson, as he made good on his commitment to leave the room early if the conference proceeded with its election. “What I didn’t agree with was holding the election right away, giving nobody an opportunity to really challenge any leadership position.”.

It has been revealed that “Part of the concern here is who wants the job? God bless him for serving,” Johnson added.

The conference conversation Tuesday morning turned into an “open-mic” with both conservatives and those who lost their elections speaking, according to senators.

Sources indicate that sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., told reporters, “To rush into this and to just ratify all the same leadership — I mean, what message does that send?”.

Recent findings suggest that but no contender to Thune emerged despite the angst, and a motion to proceed to the election, introduced by Thune’s fellow South Dakotan Sen. Mike Rounds, was accepted.

Industry observers note that sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., said voters who rejected Republicans last week were reacting to high gas prices, the war in Iran and the cost of living, not to how Senate leaders were running the conference.

“I don’t think anybody in Texas who voted for the Democrat governor was voting against John Thune. If you diagnose that as a problem, you’re misdiagnosing the problem,” Paul remarked.

Whip John Barrasso, R-Wyo., was reelected to his position, as was the chairman of the Senate Republican Conference, Tom Cotton of Arkansas. Sen. James Lankford of Oklahoma was again selected as vice chair of the conference, while Sen. Shelley Moore Capito of West Virginia was reelected as Republican Policy Committee chair.

“Our first step is to make sure the American people know that we heard what they noted, and the American people’s priorities are our priorities. That’s the way we regain their trust,” Barrasso said afterward.

Sen. Bernie Moreno of Ohio got the nod to chair the National Republican Senatorial Committee, meaning he will helm the campaign arm as the party looks ahead to the uncertain waters of 2028.

Moreno said, “I was in the retail automobile business, so when you don’t listen to your customers, your customers punish you. I think we have to own it, and I think we have to learn from it.”.

It has been revealed that sen. John Kennedy, R-La., said on Monday evening, “What we as a conference right now need is honesty. We need focus. We need to try to reach a consensus on what we need to change.”.

Kennedy was among those pushing to delay the leadership elections and told reporters on Tuesday he voted present instead of yes on whether to proceed to them.

Recent findings suggest that sen. Rick Scott, R-Fla., who ran for GOP leader twice — once in 2022 against Sen. Mitch McConnell, R-Ky., and in 2024 against Thune — declined to run again to challenge Thune. But in a Dear Colleague letter on Monday, he detailed what he’d like to see in the lame-duck session before Democrats take power, including confirming every nominee President Donald Trump has sent to the Senate, funding the government without an omnibus, banning stock trading, passing the permitting bill that is advancing this week in the Senate, passing the National Defense Authorization Act, balancing the budget and pushing through a sweeping voter ID bill known as the SAVE America Act.

Senate Republicans on Tuesday also voted on a resolution on their path forward that was spurred by a motion from Scott, aides said.

“It is the sense of the GOP Conference that we will maximize the 54 days we have with congressional majorities, to confirm every judicial nominee and every executive nominee that the conference approves of, to pass our core Republican priorities, and to do everything humanly possible to pass a reconciliation bill before Jan. 3,” the resolution reads in part.

That long list of goals highlights the expectations Thune has faced as leader, where he led one-third of Republicans’ trifecta in Washington. In the next Congress, Democrats will hold the majority in both chambers of Congress after their larger-than-expected wins, while Trump finishes out his term as president.

Thune said he told his conference: “As I look back on the last couple of years, my question is, what would you have me do differently?”.

“Given the constraints we had to deal with, all the stuff that was coming at us on a daily basis, a narrow margin in the House, the White House, the Democrats over here who were obstructing two long government shutdowns — I think we came out of it as well as could have been expected, and got a lot of stuff done,” Thune told reporters.

Sources indicate that “If you believe the exit polls, it was the war, it was the economy, it was inflation, it was fuel prices,” Thune added. “So no, I wasn’t apologizing for anything that we did. And I think on the political side, I don’t know what else I could have done.”.

#7091. A brain region known for listening helps us speak

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (651 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencenews ↗ Open Full Page

A brain region known for listening helps us speak

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (651 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencenews

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • WASHINGTON — A part of the brain famous for listening is important for talking, too.
  • Data collected from people as they listen and try to talk show that this brain region, a small spot inside a larger area called Wernicke’s area, has a more expansive job than researchers thought when it comes to communicating.
  • Sources indicate that A small part of the brain, just above the left ear, was first described in 1874 by a neurologist Carl Wernicke as necessary for making sense of speech.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

WASHINGTON — A part of the brain famous for listening is important for talking, too.

Data collected from people as they listen and try to talk show that this brain region, a small spot inside a larger area called Wernicke’s area, has a more expansive job than researchers thought when it comes to communicating. The results may help efforts to restore people’s voices. The results presented November 15 at the annual meeting of the Society for Neuroscience and published November 19 in Science.The study provides convincing evidence that this brain spot is critical for speech production, says neurologist and language researcher Jeffrey Binder of the Medical College of Wisconsin in Milwaukee. “My hope is that this study will help scientists and clinicians accept a more accurate interpretation of this focal area” as an early stop on the pathway to saying a word.

Sources indicate that A small part of the brain, just above the left ear, was first described in 1874 by a neurologist Carl Wernicke as necessary for making sense of speech. People with damage there had trouble comprehending words. But some people also had trouble producing them. “Sounds were swapped, words were replaced with near misses,” Edward Chang of the University of California, San Francisco, stated in a news briefing. “The basic question has been, ‘Why would damage to a hearing area of the brain break the ability to speak?’ That question has been open for 150 years.”The new research offers an answer: A small bit of Wernicke’s area (to be extremely specific, the left posterior superior temporal gyrus or lpSTG ) becomes active just before a word is spoken. “Every word that you have said today began in that small part above your left ear about a quarter of a second before you said it,” Chang said.

The finding adds to growing evidence that brain areas are more complex than people have appreciated, notes neuroscientist Leigh Hochberg at Brown University in Providence, R.I. “I believe that one of the things we are going to learn over the next five, 10 years of this research, is that each part of the brain that, we were taught as a med student or a grad student, does this, probably does that and a whole lot more.”.

Scientists measured brain activity in 28 people before they had surgery for epilepsy or tumors. They were able to see that this brain region kicked on as a person listened to words, and also just before they attempted to speak. Cells there had preferences for certain sorts of words, long ones, for instance. “It’s more active when you’re about to say the word caterpillar than when you’re about to say the word cat,” said Matthew Leonard, a cognitive neuroscientist at UCSF.

Recent findings suggest that electrical stimulation to this small bit of brain also interfered with people’s ability to talk. “What we found was that stimulation, really only in this lpSTG area, disrupted this speech production when it was delivered just prior to speaking,” said UCSF bioengineer Alexander Silva.

It has been revealed that some efforts to make implanted devices that can help restore speech to people who no longer talk focus on the motor cortex, a part of the brain that controls the movements required for speech. This bit of Wernicke’s area offers an additional spot to consider, Silva said. “What if you could target a single brain region and gain access to the full spectrum of speech, from listening all the way up to speech production?”.

Experimental brain implants in two volunteers with paralysis were able to detect both what they heard and what they were trying to say, the researchers report in the study.

The discovery may help scientists better understand situations that involve both hearing and speaking, such as speech or comprehension differences in people with autism, or how children first begin learning to talk, Chang said.

Grand Theft Auto Started as a Broken Racing Game No One Liked. Then the Code Malfunctioned—Brilliantly.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review.
  • Sources indicate that it’s spanned the lifecycle of countless gaming consoles, survived multiple scandals, and even withstood a Congressional investigation.
  • Industry observers note that yet, the massive franchise was almost over before it began.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us?

Sources indicate that it’s spanned the lifecycle of countless gaming consoles, survived multiple scandals, and even withstood a Congressional investigation. The Grand Theft Auto franchise is seemingly unkillable. Not even a more-than-a-decade wait for the latest installment, Grand Theft Auto VI, could dull the rabid hunger the global gaming community has for the series of open world crime games.

Industry observers note that yet, the massive franchise was almost over before it began. The original Grand Theft Auto, it turns out, was on the proverbial chopping block in the middle of its development. It was only through a few fateful glitches that developers saw what they really had on their hands.

Recent findings suggest that “It was awful,” former creative director Gary Penn recalled in an interview quoted by Game Informer. “It never really felt like it was going anywhere.” At the time, in 1994, the game wasn’t even called Grand Theft Auto,—it went by the much tamer moniker Race’n’Chase. Its developers, now known as Rockstar North, were then a small Scottish studio called DMA Design Ltd. They were best known at the time for a cute, family-friendly (if mildly macabre) PC game called Lemmings.

According to recent reports, “The aim of Race’n’Chase,” read a March 1995 design document, “...is to produce a fun, addictive and fast multi-player car racing and crashing game which uses a novel graphics method.” The problem was, the game they were working on was neither fun nor addictive. The car crashes, for one, were a nightmare. “They just didn’t work,” programmer Mike Dailly told The Guardian. “The code was like spaghetti junction.”.

Then there was the matter of the game’s central premise. Originally, Race’n’Chase was meant to be a top-down game where you could play as either the criminals or the police in pursuit, but the developers found that the latter element needed to be excised “’cause nobody wanted to play the cops.”.

According to recent reports, even worse, as the developers tried to deal these design challenges, they were missing key deadlines, and their counterparts in America were getting impatient. “Every week they wanted to kill this game,” recalled level designer Paul Farley in a video for The Guardian. “We’d have to kind of argue to keep it going.”.

Industry observers note that then something broke. And it was the best thing that ever happened to them.

The game had refocused around the criminal element, with the police now pursuing the player in a manner inspired by, of all things, the ghosts in Pac-Man. “Then one day,” Penn recounted, “I think it was a bug, the police suddenly became mental and aggressive. Everybody suddenly went, ‘Hey this is actually pretty cool. There’s something in this, this is working.’”.

In a recent development, that malfunction switched things from Pac-Man ghosts to maniac cops—and recontextualized the entire game in the developers’ minds. “It was less about the mission stuff, which we always thought was another mess, and more about just general play—just being able to p**s around.”.

Recent findings suggest that the developers leaned into the freedom of the game’s sprawling digital city, focusing less on what players could accomplish and more on what they could get away with. In that moment, Race’n’Chase became Grand Theft Auto in all but name. Team members went home at night to watch American action fare like Speed and The A-Team, then came back the next day to pitch scenes from them as missions players could pick up at Liberty City’s trademark phone booths. Most importantly, they started seeing bugs not as roadblocks, but as launching pads.

Recent findings suggest that later in development, another glitch caused groups of NPC pedestrians to “start following one person around,” Farley recalled, much like the marching creatures in DMA’s previous hit, Lemmings. “We thought: ‘Can we use this? What sort of people walk around in a long line like that?’ And we thought of Hare Krishnas.” Rather than do some drastic rewrite of the code, they just tweaked the look of the pedestrians’ sprites, and got the game out to the public.

It has been revealed that the game was famously met with controversy after its release because of its violent content, but that uproar actually played into the game’s marketing, and it became a massive financial success for the small Scottish studio. Grand Theft Auto has gone on to become one of the best-selling video game franchises in history, a title sure to be cemented with the release of the notably “sick day inducing” Grand Theft Auto VI.

And none of it would have happened without a single, fateful glitch.

His stories for the Enthusiast Group have involved coordinating with organizations like the National Parks Service and the Secret Service, and travelling to notable historical sites and archaeological digs, from excavations of America’ earliest colonies to the former homes of Edgar Allan Poe.

Latest Update: Threats to broadcasters hang over FCC nominee hearing

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1046 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, FCC nominee Danielle Thumann Severs waits to testify during her confirmation hearing with the Senate Commerce Committee on Tuesday.
  • President Donald Trump's Republican nominee to the Federal Communications Commission faced opposition Tuesday from Senate Democrats who fear the commission could be controlled exclusively by Republicans under Chairman Brendan Carr, who they vowed to investigate in the next Congress.
  • Appearing before the Senate Commerce Committee, nominee Danielle Thumann Severs limited her commitments to independence from Carr, including on regulating broadcasters based on their content decisions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, FCC nominee Danielle Thumann Severs waits to testify during her confirmation hearing with the Senate Commerce Committee on Tuesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

President Donald Trump's Republican nominee to the Federal Communications Commission faced opposition Tuesday from Senate Democrats who fear the commission could be controlled exclusively by Republicans under Chairman Brendan Carr, who they vowed to investigate in the next Congress.

Appearing before the Senate Commerce Committee, nominee Danielle Thumann Severs limited her commitments to independence from Carr, including on regulating broadcasters based on their content decisions.

Much of the hearing focused on Carr and his threats to use the FCC to punish broadcasters he disagrees with.

In a recent development, sen. Ben Ray Luján, D-N.M., remarked that he expects Carr will not last long in his position once Democrats take control of Congress in the latest year.

“Mr. Carr, if you're listening now, know you're going to be in this body once a month, if not more, and in the House of Representatives as well, answering questions … so we can get to the bottom of the nonsense and the cover-ups that have been taking place,” Luján noted.

According to recent reports, the nomination of Thumann Severs, who currently serves as senior counsel to Carr, has led to consternation among Democrats due to continued vacancies at the FCC. The five-member commission is intended to have three members of the president’s party, including the chair, and two in the minority.

Recent findings suggest that right now Carr serves alongside fellow Republican Olivia Trusty and Democrat Anna M. Gomez, whose term expired earlier this year. Gomez may continue to serve through next year under the law if a replacement is not nominated and confirmed.

Democrats are concerned that if Thumann Severs were to be confirmed, the commission’s three Republican members could constitute a quorum on their own, allowing Trump to fire Gomez.

Sen. John Hickenlooper, D-Colo., said Senate precedent is to move pairs of one Democratic and one Republican nominee for the FCC and that he “strongly” believed the Thumann Severs nomination should have been paired with a renomination of Gomez in order to continue having “both parties at the table.”.

“A bipartisan FCC is essential to avoid things like large-scale media consolidation [and] I think also, more fundamentally, to protect a free and diverse press [that] serves everyone,” Hickenlooper mentioned.

In addition to urging Trump to renominate Gomez, Democrats underlined the need for a second Democratic member of the commission.

Hickenlooper highlighted Thumann Severs’ close work with Carr, who Democrats and some Republicans have been critical of for comments about using the FCC’s public interest standard against television stations airing programming Carr disagrees with.

Thumann Severs’ work at the FCC currently focuses on the Wireline, Public Safety and Homeland Security, and Consumer and Governmental Affairs bureaus, rather than the Media Bureau.

Sources indicate that committee Chair Ted Cruz, R-Texas, has also been critical of Carr’s comments. On Tuesday, he listed the FCC’s request for ABC-owned stations to submit early license renewals alongside earlier incidents in which he said Democrats encouraged the weaponization of the FCC against conservative voices.

“The First Amendment places important limits on the government’s ability to regulate speech,” Cruz mentioned. “The FCC possesses significant regulatory authority over communications, so there is always a risk that it could weaponize its authority against Americans with whom it disagrees.”.

Thumann Severs committed to Cruz that she would base licensing decisions on “the law and the record” and not use the FCC’s authority to “pressure or punish” broadcasters for protected speech.

However, when Sen. Edward J. Markey, D-Mass., questioned Thumann Severs on whether the FCC could punish broadcasters the president disagreed with, Thumann Severs repeated one of Carr’s arguments in discussing the FCC’s role.

Sources indicate that “Broadcasters are subject to public interest obligations as part of the public trustee model in exchange for the licenses that they hold,” she noted. “As part of those public interest obligations, they are subject to many different rules and requirements, and the FCC is charged with enforcing and investigating the public interest standard against broadcasters.”.

Under repeated questions from Markey about Carr’s previous remarks, Thumann Severs noted she would base her decisions “in the facts and the law and the record.”.

Recent findings suggest that luján also asked Thumann Severs to name issues where she had disagreed with Carr or Trump. While she said her decisions would be her own, she declined to name any examples of disagreement.

In addition to questions about Carr, Democrats asked the nominee about the FCC’s E-Rate program, which provides low-cost connectivity for schools and libraries, and the Universal Service Fund, which funds the E-Rate program and other programs.

Thumann Severs remarked that she believes the E-Rate program has been successful and that the FCC has a statutory obligation to provide some kind of discounted service to schools and libraries. But she was less forthcoming on whether the FCC could shut down the program as it currently exists without congressional approval or whether the program should be restricted only to rural areas.

Late last month, Democratic members of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, led by Communications and Technology Subcommittee ranking member Doris Matsui, D-Calif., sent a letter to Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., and Cruz urging Gomez’s renomination with any move to confirm a Republican nominee.

“Commissioner Gomez has shown the experience and judgment to continue that work,” the members wrote. “We therefore ask that the Senate pair any upcoming Republican nominee with her renomination to a full term, consistent with the bipartisan design Congress built into this agency.”.

On Monday, the Leadership Conference on Civil and Human Rights also sent a letter to committee leadership urging a delay on the hearing and any vote on Thumann Severs’ nomination until Gomez can be renominated.

“Independent agencies should not be extensions of presidential will: their leaders should exercise independent judgement based on their expertise and statutory mandates,” the group wrote.

Cruz did not indicate Tuesday when the committee might vote on Thumann Severs’ nomination, and no markup has yet been announced by the committee of hers' and those of three others for two posts at NASA and one at the Transportation Department who also testified.

Solo meerkats can find their way back home

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (415 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Sciencenews

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It was a hot, dry day in the Kalahari Desert, and Mathilde Martin was running after a meerkat.
  • The animal wore a GPS tracker around its neck and bolted between shelters, like an action hero running for cover, claims Martin, a biologist at the University of Zurich.
  • Sources indicate that the answer was quite well, the researchers reported November 19 in the Journal of Experimental Biology.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It was a hot, dry day in the Kalahari Desert, and Mathilde Martin was running after a meerkat.

The animal wore a GPS tracker around its neck and bolted between shelters, like an action hero running for cover, claims Martin, a biologist at the University of Zurich. She and her colleagues had captured the meerkat earlier that morning, driven it 1.5 kilometers from its pack and then released it into the desert. They were trying to find out how well individual meerkats could find their way back home.

Sources indicate that the answer was quite well, the researchers reported November 19 in the Journal of Experimental Biology. The results suggest that meerkats can navigate expertly on their own, perhaps relying on mental maps charted early in life. “They all seem to be very, very good,” Martin says. It’s a surprise finding for a species known for its group cooperation.

Sources indicate that meerkats (Suricata suricatta), which live in southern Africa, form tight-knit family groups of up to 50 members. These social animals cooperate in many aspects of life, including by babysitting each other’s pups and watching for predators while traveling along foraging paths. Martin and her colleagues thought meerkats might also rely on one another for navigating. Some pack members, perhaps those who’ve had more opportunity to explore solo, might have spatial knowledge of their territory and lead the rest, she says. But that’s not what the team discovered.

According to recent reports, in separate catch and release experiments with 20 individual meerkats, 18 made a beeline back home, back to their group or back to the site where they were captured. (The other two may have been too stressed to get moving, Martin says.).

Recent findings suggest that neither age nor individual experience, which researchers had been tracking, seemed to factor into the meerkats’ homing skills. Nearly all of them knew where to go, Martin notes. She thinks these crackerjack navigators relied on visual cues to orient themselves. They’d pop up on their hind legs and scan the landscape before scampering off in a direct line to their target.

Sources indicate that it’s likely that scent played a role, too, though distant scent marks may have faded by the time the meerkats were released. The researchers dropped the animals off in territory they hadn’t visited for at least 30 days. “Otherwise,” she indicates, “it would have been a bit too easy for them to find their way back,” she says.

Latest Update: Rift grows among Senate Democrats over who will lead in majority

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bernie Sanders and Elissa Slotkin hold a news conference calling for a “bold direction” for Senate Democrats on Tuesday.
  • According to recent reports, more Democrats emerged Tuesday wanting someone besides Senate Democratic leader Charles E.
  • Industry observers note that but Schumer maintained confidence he would be reelected to the post despite Sens.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, sens. Bernie Sanders and Elissa Slotkin hold a news conference calling for a “bold direction” for Senate Democrats on Tuesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

According to recent reports, more Democrats emerged Tuesday wanting someone besides Senate Democratic leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., to lead their conference in the majority.

Industry observers note that but Schumer maintained confidence he would be reelected to the post despite Sens. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., and Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., publicly calling for a different leader or a “concrete initiative” that provides change.

Sources indicate that “I’m confident I will be elected majority leader, and our caucus is really united in focusing on bringing down costs, on ending the corruption, on ending the chaos, on ending the war,” Schumer told reporters Tuesday. “We have great unity in our caucus, and I’ll be proud to lead it.”.

Sanders stated during a news conference Tuesday the election was about “change and the need for the Democratic Party to move in a upcoming and bold direction.”.

“I personally have known Chuck Schumer for over 30 years, and I like Chuck. Nobody works harder than Chuck Schumer. But in my view the time is now for change, and I will not be supporting Chuck to be reelected as the Democratic leader,” Sanders said, calling for an “economy that works for all, not just the people on top.”.

In a recent development, “Do I think Chuck has been leading in that direction?” he asked. “No.”.

Recent findings suggest that some incoming members and now incumbents have pointed to Maryland Democrat Chris Van Hollen as one possibility to challenge Schumer. Van Hollen had previously thrown cold water on the idea by saying he was instead “kicking the tires” on a presidential run in 2028 but has recently changed his tune.

A person familiar with Van Hollen’s thinking noted he “has received an outpouring of calls on running for majority leader and is now in active listening mode.”.

Slotkin did not endorse anyone for leader but said she had a “really productive conversation” with Van Hollen yesterday.

Recent findings suggest that “Whoever wants my vote is going to have to show me a concrete plan that’s definitely different. I’m a ‘no’ until and unless I see that from anyone,” she said, urging her peers to “withhold quorum” when Senate Democrats hold their leadership elections “until you get that plan and you feel like you have a voice in that plan.”.

Sources indicate that she urged not just a roadmap for the first 100 days, but ideas for how to “communicate differently.” As for her own future, she noted, “I am not actively seeking this job. I’m seeking change.”.

Asked about his plans Monday evening, Van Hollen noted, “It’s not about me, but I am listening to the thousands of people who have been calling for change, but especially listening to our members, with a particular ear to fresh members who have just come off the campaign trail.”.

Industry observers note that “What I’ve noted from the very beginning is, we shouldn’t have a coronation. We should have a caucus discussion about what we're going to do with the power and responsibilities that have been invested in us,” Van Hollen said. “I’m in listening mode and haven’t shut the door.”.

Van Hollen took it a step further at an event Tuesday in Washington, D.C., criticizing the minority leader and Democrats’ campaign arm over their preferences in some primaries. “Schumer and the DSCC sided with the crypto industry and AIPAC against these candidates,” he mentioned, according to a livestream of the event.

Schumer tried to tamp down the suggestion of a rivalry. “We talk frequently, and we’re united — united in lowering costs, and united in ending this damn war,” he stated of Van Hollen.

Others threw their support behind Schumer ahead of the Democratic leadership elections, which are expected to take place in December.

Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee Chair Kirsten Gillibrand, D-N.Y., praised Schumer for raising money and recruiting candidates like Sens.-elect Sherrod Brown of Ohio and Roy Cooper of North Carolina to help land at minimum seven seats, and potentially nine if Alaska and Mississippi ultimately swing their way.

According to recent reports, “That takes vision. It takes clarity of thought. It takes strategic leadership, and that is what Sen. Schumer has done. And that is why you will see, despite all grumblings, enormous gratitude,” she noted.

Gillibrand pointed to candidates like Scott Colom, the Democrat in Mississippi who is currently leading GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in a nail-biter of a race. “That wave doesn’t get created by magic. It gets created by hard work and putting the pieces together over years,” she said.

Colom, however, has been noncommittal, telling MS NOW, “Too many of our leaders are from the same areas of the country,” pointing to the Brooklyn roots of both Schumer and current House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, who is expected to run for speaker on the House side.

Sen. Ruben Gallego, D-Ariz., said he and Schumer have had their differences. But he implied he backs him for majority leader: “At the end of the day, these are historic numbers. It’s time for us to unify. We are going to work together as a caucus to plan together about how to move forward for what the country wants us to do, and I think we have the person who I think is going to lead us there.”.

Industry observers note that sen. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., noted Democrats have “an opportunity to do things differently, and I think we will, regardless of who the leader is. It doesn’t really matter whose name is on the door.”.

“Yes,” he said of his support for Schumer, noting that so far, nobody has officially stepped up to the plate. “This is a guy that worked incredibly hard over the last couple of years. I know people have other opinions about this. But we have a mandate to do things and get things done for the American people.”.

“And we can do that with Chuck Schumer.”.

Industry observers note that mark Schoeff Jr., Paul M. Krawzak and Kelly Livingston contributed to this report.

#7080. How to Strategy a Trip to the World’s Largest Ski Resort, Les Trois Vallées

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (2097 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cntraveler ↗ Open Full Page

How to Strategy a Trip to the World’s Largest Ski Resort, Les Trois Vallées

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2097 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cntraveler

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that standing at the top of a steep gully, I looked down at the line ahead.
  • Industry observers note that before I dropped in, I looked out at the view ahead.
  • Les Trois Vallées (also known as Les 3 Vallées, or the 3 Valleys) began with the construction of a 19-passenger open-air “chairlift” in 1938 in the small town of Méribel.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that standing at the top of a steep gully, I looked down at the line ahead. A handful of tracks cut through 10 inches of powder to my left, telling the story of the skiers who arrived before me. But I couldn’t help but notice untouched snow under an overhanging cliff face to my right.

Industry observers note that before I dropped in, I looked out at the view ahead. I could make out tiny chairlift towers on the snow-capped peaks and ridgelines on the horizon. It felt as if the entire mountain range belonged to the Les Trois Vallées Ski Resort, one of the best—and the biggest—ski destinations in Europe.

Les Trois Vallées (also known as Les 3 Vallées, or the 3 Valleys) began with the construction of a 19-passenger open-air “chairlift” in 1938 in the small town of Méribel. But it wasn’t until 1971, with the creation of the joint ski pass that offers access to the seven resorts that make up Les Trois Vallées, that the ski area took its current form.

In a recent development, today, the resort spans three main valleys and has 169 chairlifts accessing nearly 26,000 acres of skiable terrain (for comparison, Park City has 7,300 acres of skiable terrain). That makes it the world’s largest interconnected ski area—and it’s all accessible via a single ski ticket. Lift tickets for each of the seven resorts are available, but the cost savings don’t make it worthwhile—for a couple of extra euros, you can buy a pass that gives you access to the entire resort. Les Trois Vallées is also a convenient destination for Epic Pass holders, who get seven days of skiing at Les Trois Vallées.

Given the destination is so vast, here are some tips for navigating the expansive terrain and various villages that make up Les Trois Vallées, based on my most recent trip in 2026.

An aerial view of the skiing area of Les Trois Vallees, also known as The 3 Valleys.

“We need to ski over there today,” our guide and former ski racer, Timothée “Timy” Theaux, notes as he pointed toward a distant ridgeline. “The wind is coming from Italy, so that side of the ridge is where we’ll find the best snow.”.

We skied seamlessly from lift to lift until we reached an open bowl with untouched powder. Theaux knew exactly where to go given the current conditions, and how to get there.

Les Trois Vallées isn’t like a typical US resort. The terrain is so vast and complex that skiing it without a guide can be more of a chore than skiing with one. Guides—which you can hire through each resort’s ski school, like ESF Val Thorens—not only know how to navigate the resort and keep you safe off-piste, but also know exactly where to go to score skiers the best possible conditions and overall experience.

It has been revealed that I pictured myself without a guide at the resort, spending day after day staring at trail maps, hopping on lifts that dropped me a mile from where I thought they would. Thankfully, our guide’s expertise spared us from what could’ve been a logistical nightmare.

Recent findings suggest that on our third day at the resort, low visibility made it hard to see more than 15 feet ahead. As we impatiently waited for the fog to lift, lapping groomed runs outside of our hotel, Theaux decided to head toward Courchevel.

“Courchevel and Méribel are good to ski when visibility is low,” he told us, explaining that they’re both at a lower elevation and have more tree skiing.

According to recent reports, even if it’s just for a day or two, hiring a guide at the beginning of the trip will help skiers and riders get a feel for Les Trois Vallées and each individual resort. While all seven resorts offer a good mix of terrain for every ability level, some, like Val Thorens, sit at a higher elevation and have more alpine terrain than resorts like Courchevel, which are lower and have more tree skiing.

The terrain is also so vast that it’s not hard to avoid crowds—which typically stick to the pistes at each resort (Courchevel, Val Thorens, and Méribel are some of the more popular ones). Focusing on one resort per day, rather than spending an entire day riding lifts from one side of the resort to the other, is a stellar way to maximize time on snow.

Backcountry skiers can enjoy the vast off-piste areas beyond the resort's groomed runs.

Industry observers note that unlike many US ski areas, there aren’t dedicated off-piste areas marked on a map—everything within (and really, outside of) the resort’s boundaries is fair game. But leaving the pistes requires a guide, or at the very least, knowledge of how to navigate backcountry terrain. A low-angle, mellow backcountry slope can promptly steepen enough to raise avalanche concerns, and skiers who leave the pistes should be able to recognize and manage backcountry hazards. And while not all off-piste terrain at Les Trois Vallées requires the chops of an expert skier, it doesn’t take much to get yourself in trouble. When it came to navigating the resort, keeping us out of trouble, and scoring the best conditions away from the crowds, Theaux took out all of the guesswork.

After several lift rides and traverses, we finally found ourselves in Courchevel, on the opposite side of the resort from where we were staying in Val Thorens. We immediately left the groomed runs and headed for the trees, leaving the crowded pistes behind.

Recent findings suggest that as a New Englander, I feel at home in tight, scrappy tree runs. But leaving the pistes to explore the vast terrain and big lines encompassed by Les Trois Vallées was special. Unlike the runs I’ve grown accustomed to at my local ski areas, pistes at Les Trois Vallées don’t have a hard line defined by thick trees and icy trail edges; almost everything is skiable.

Sources indicate that “Dropping into an off-piste line alone, with just your guide, is one of the most special feelings in the world,” says Dan Egan, a pro skier who has been spending winters in France for nearly three decades. He was skiing with us for the week. “You really get to connect with the place in a way you never would on a groomed run filled with people.”.

Sources indicate that at the top of nearly every chairlift, I spotted about a dozen distant backcountry lines I wanted to explore. Saw-toothed peaks gave way to steep chutes and couloirs, many of which funneled into open powder fields. “I need to come back and ski that,” I found myself thinking about a dozen times per day.

Courchevel is perhaps the spiffiest resort at The Three Valleys—but there are budget-friendly villages nearby.

Each resort town has its own feel, so it’s important to know your priorities before booking. Courchevel, for example, is the most luxurious destination, while Col de la Chambre is perfect for skiers who want to spend their evenings partying. Budget-conscious skiers should consider Brides-les-Bains or Orelle; whereas Les Menuires might be better for families. Saint-Martin and Méribel both have a cozy European village vibe, but Méribel might have the slight advantage for off-piste skiers.

Val Thorens is known for its vibrant aprés-ski scene.

Recent findings suggest that when we first arrived at the Fahrenheit Seven hotel in Val Thorens, I felt like I was in an early 2000s ski movie. The back deck was packed shoulder to shoulder, and the DJ knew just what to play to keep the crowd going. It was the middle of the afternoon on a random Sunday.

Recent findings suggest that while there is plenty of partying to be done all over Les Trois Vallées (the parties at La Folie Douce Val Thorens and La Folie Douce Méribel are not to be missed), there are also more laid-back places to stay. Of the seven resorts and villages, each has its own unique feel and caters to different types of skiers. And all of them offer lift access to the pistes.

In a recent development, “Courchevel is my favorite place to ski because it has a lot of luxury restaurants and accommodations, so hardcore skiers think it’s not for them,” Theaux told us during our low-visibility day. “The off-piste terrain is always empty.”.

But if you’re heading to Courchevel for the accommodations over the skiing, Les Airelles Courchevel is about as luxurious as it gets.

Recent findings suggest that saint-Martin-de-Belleville, slightly below Val Thorens in the Belleville Valley, has the quiet feel of a quaint European hamlet. Like Val Thorens (and most villages around the resort), it’s very walkable, but it's better for skiers who value history and culture over parties. Orelle, made up of 10 hamlets and less popular than other villages, and Brides-les-Bains, known for its thermal waters and spa culture, are also quiet options; the latter is great for budget-conscious travelers.

Méribel, next to Courchevel's high-end restaurants and parties, is known as a family-friendly resort village with plenty of restaurants, bars, shops, and easy lift access. Similarly, Les Menuires is also known as a family destination, but is ideal for skiers looking to explore some of Les Trois Vallées’ bigger off-piste terrain.

Food across the resort is locally sourced, even at on-hill dining options, like Caron 3200.

No matter which village you stay in, good food is never more than a couple of steps or a chairlift ride away.

In a recent development, “I really love the jamon because it requires patience,” notes Vincent Suchet, the cheesemaker and grandson of Pépé Nicolas at family-owned, Michelin-starred Chez Pépé Nicolas—located just below Val Thorens in the Belleville Valley. He told us as we sipped wine and tasted local cheeses in a cool, stone-walled cellar: “And I favor the cheeses because you have to wait two years; the flavor is the best when you have to wait.”.

The culinary experience stood in stark contrast to what I was used to at US ski areas—fast service, overpriced, yet mediocre cheeseburgers and pizza, and ingredients sourced hundreds, if not thousands, of miles away. At Les Trois Vallées, home to ten Michelin-starred restaurants like Hotel La Bouitte, the food is just as notable as the skiing.

Recent findings suggest that during my week at the resort, I couldn’t find a single fast-food or chain restaurant in any of the seven villages. Restaurants are all family-owned, and thought goes into where ingredients are sourced. It’s not uncommon for cheeses to be made by a local farmer whose family has been doing it for generations.

Caron 3200, perched above Val Thorens, is the highest wine bar in Europe.

Even on-hill dining options, like Caron 3200, perched above Val Thorens at 10,500 feet (making it the highest wine bar in Europe), emphasize the culinary experience.

It has been revealed that “We have 150 different wines, and most are French,” Eric Bonnel, managing director of Val Thorens Tours, told us as we sipped wine and admired the views of Mont Blanc and the surrounding Alps through the oversized windows. “And we store them at three different altitudes. The reds are aged at a higher altitude because there’s less oxygen.”.

Industry observers note that on our last evening at Les Trois Vallées, it finally started snowing. I momentarily felt a slight sense of disappointment about leaving ahead of a huge storm. But as I sipped my post-meal Génépi with new and old friends, I realized it didn’t matter. The skiing was only a small part of the Les Trois Vallées experience.

Les Trois Vallées is accessible via train, plane, or car.

Sources indicate that for international travelers, the most convenient airport to fly into is Geneva, which is located just a couple of hours from the resort (depending on where you’re staying). While the Swiss airport has the most international flight options, it’s also possible to fly into Lyon, Chambéry, and Grenoble.

Sources indicate that companies like Alpine Fleet offer shuttle transfers from the airports to the resorts in Les Trois Vallées. You can also rent a car, but with the lifts and shuttles available in each resort town, you don’t really need one once you arrive.

Those traveling within Europe or from one of the area’s international airports can access Les Trois Vallées by train, with the Moûtiers﻿ train station serving major cities like London, Paris, Geneva, and Lyon. From the train station, travelers can get to each resort by taxi or bus.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Carnival Cruise Line has opened bookings for the Carnival Sunrise, Sunshine and Valor’s 2028-29 season sailing from Latest Orleans, Galveston, Miami and Mobile.

The schedule includes more than 160 itineraries ranging from four-day getaways to 14-day Carnival Journeys cruises and offers opportunities to visit 21 destinations across The Bahamas, Caribbean, Mexico and Central America.

Highlights include the Sunrise expanding Miami operations, the Sunshine going year-round in Galveston and the Valor featuring extended Carnival Journeys cruises from Mobile.

More than 50 sailings across the three ships will visit Carnival’s exclusive destination Celebration Key, which the manufacturer expects will welcome 3.5 million guests in 2027.

The Carnival Sunrise will open the deployment with a spring season from Miami beginning in April 2028, offering four- to eight-day sailings visiting The Bahamas and Caribbean and calling at Celebration Key, Nassau, Grand Turk, Ocho Rios, Grand Cayman, Cozumel, Aruba, Bonaire, Curacao and RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay.

Starting June 2028, the ship will reposition to Newly introduced Orleans, from where it will offer six-, seven-, eight- and nine-day cruises to The Bahamas and Western Caribbean year round, visiting destinations such as Celebration Key, Nassau, Key West, Cozumel, Belize, Grand Cayman, Montego Bay and Isla Tropicale.

The cruise line underlined a series of seven-day Bahamas cruises featuring Celebration Key, Nassau and Key West as a highlight.

The Sunrise will also operate a 14-day Carnival Journeys cruise to the Caribbean and Panama, visiting Aruba, Curaçao, Cartagena, Colón and Limón.

The Carnival Sunshine will operate year-round from Galveston for the first time, with 29 four-day cruises to Cozumel or Progreso, as well as 24 10-day voyages to the Western Caribbean, Eastern Caribbean and Caribbean and Panama.

Select Eastern Caribbean itineraries feature calls to Celebration Key, Grand Turk, Amber Cove and RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay.

The Carnival Valor will continue offering six-, seven- and eight-day itineraries from Mobile to The Bahamas and Western Caribbean, including sailings to Celebration Key, Nassau, Bimini, RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay, Cozumel, Belize, Grand Cayman, Montego Bay and Ocho Rios.

There will also be two 14-day Carnival Journeys voyages: a Caribbean and Panama itinerary visiting Aruba, Curaçao, Cartagena, Colón and Limón, and a Southern Caribbean itinerary calling at San Juan, Aruba, Curaçao, Amber Cove, Grand Cayman and Ocho Rios.

  • Bernie Moreno will chair the National Republican Senatorial Committee during the 2028 cycle.
  • House and Senate Republicans picked their latest campaign chiefs Tuesday, tasking Ohio Sen.

Sources indicate that ohio Sen. Bernie Moreno will chair the National Republican Senatorial Committee during the 2028 cycle. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call file photo).

House and Senate Republicans picked their latest campaign chiefs Tuesday, tasking Ohio Sen. Bernie Moreno and Georgia Rep. Brian Jack with leading the GOP campaign arms for the 2028 election cycle.

In their new positions, both will spearhead Republicans’ push to win back majorities on Capitol Hill after Democrats seized control of both chambers of Congress by flipping more than 40 House seats and at least seven Senate seats in last week’s midterm elections.

Sources indicate that republicans returned to Capitol Hill this week still reeling from their losses but resisted calls to delay Tuesday’s leadership elections. In the Senate, South Dakota’s John Thune was reelected Republican leader without any opposition, while Ohio Rep. Jim Jordan defeated Louisiana Rep. Steve Scalise in a closed-door, secret-ballot election to lead House Republicans next year.

Moreno will succeed South Carolina Sen. Tim Scott as chair of the National Republican Senatorial Committee.

“Republicans must enter this next election clear-eyed: the road ahead back to a Republican Senate majority will by no means be easy but the fight has never been so important,” the Ohio senator noted in a statement.

Speaking to reporters on Capitol Hill, Moreno described his upcoming role as “a hell of a job.” He noted Republicans would be “absolute savages” on ending government corruption and continuing “to work for the American people.”.

“I suspect the best tailwind we’ll have is that the Democrats will learn all the wrong lessons,” he told reporters.

Recent findings suggest that moreno, a close ally of President Donald Trump, is right now serving his first term. He first ran for Senate during the 2022 cycle but dropped out of a crowded GOP primary eventually won by JD Vance. Two years later, buoyed by an endorsement from Trump, he won a contested primary for the state’s other Senate seat and went on to oust Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown that fall.

According to recent reports, brown is poised to return to the Senate after defeating appointed Republican Sen. Jon Husted last week in a special election for the remaining Senate term of Vice President Vance. While Ohio has swung heavily toward Republicans over the past decade, Democrats scored massive wins in the Buckeye State last week, winning several statewide offices and flipping three seats in the U.S. House.

But assuming he runs again for a full term, Brown will be on the ballot in 2028, setting up what’s likely to be a tense home-state fight.

Sources indicate that in an apparent reference to the returning Brown, Moreno offered some Washington advice Tuesday: “Make sure you rent. Do not buy.”.

The 2028 Senate map gives Republican pickup opportunities in a handful of swing states, including Arizona, Georgia, Nevada, Latest Hampshire and Pennsylvania. The party will also be defending battleground seats in Alaska, Iowa, North Carolina and Wisconsin. Also on the Senate ballot are races for Republican-held seats in Kansas and South Carolina, where Democrats scored surprise wins last week.

Sources indicate that on the House side, Jack defeated Indiana Rep. Rudy Yakym III to become the next chairman of the National Republican Congressional Committee. He takes office after one of the worst elections for the GOP in recent decades and will succeed outgoing NRCC Chair Richard Hudson, who lost his own North Carolina seat last week.

In a recent development, house Republicans face the tough task of cutting into Democrats’ 40-plus-seat majority next cycle. But the party will have a slew of pickup opportunities, given the sheer number of seats Democrats won in historically red territory this year.

Like Moreno, Jack was first elected to Congress 2024, leveraging a close relationship with Trump to win an open seat outside Atlanta. He previously was White House director of political affairs during Trump’s first term and was a senior adviser to the president’s 2024 campaign. Over the past two years, he served as the NRCC’s recruitment chair.

Savannah Behrmann contributed to this report.

  • In a recent development, the best vacuum for your home is about more than just suction power and fancy features.
  • A vacuum that excels at pulling pet hair out of plush carpet and off of upholstered furniture might be overkill for a small apartment with mostly hardwood floors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us?

In a recent development, the best vacuum for your home is about more than just suction power and fancy features. It’s really about which type works with your floors, your cleaning habits, and the messes you deal with every day.

A vacuum that excels at pulling pet hair out of plush carpet and off of upholstered furniture might be overkill for a small apartment with mostly hardwood floors. And while a robot vacuum takes some of the work off your hands, it probably shouldn’t be your only line of defense against stubborn dirt and debris.

Sources indicate that after testing dozens of vacuums across different styles and floor types, I’ve learned that there isn’t exactly a one-size-fits-all solution. Here’s what to consider before you buy so you can find the best model, whether you have wall-to-wall carpeting, hardwood, tile, or a little bit of everything.

According to recent reports, carpet tends to hold quite a bit of dirt, dust, crumbs, and pet hair, so you’ll want a vacuum with enough agitation and suction to pull debris from in between the fibers. An upright vacuum, such as the Shark AZ2002 Vertex, is often a good choice, particularly if you have large carpeted rooms or thicker pile. Its motorized brush roll helps lift embedded dirt and hair, while a high-capacity dustbin or bag means fewer trips to the trash can. A sealed filtration system and HEPA filter are worth considering if you’re worried about fine dust and allergens.

A canister vacuum is another strong option, especially if you have stairs, area rugs, or a mix of carpet and hard flooring. These models offer a separate motorized floorhead or interchangeable attachments, giving you more flexibility than a traditional upright vacuum. They’re not always the easiest to store because of extended hoses and extra pieces, but they’re workhorses.

Shark AZ2002 Vertex Powered Lift-Away Upright Vacuum.

Miele Classic C1 Turbo Team Bagged Canister Vacuum.

Bissell Pet Hair Eraser Allergen Lift-Off Upright Vacuum.

Recent findings suggest that for homes with mostly hardwood, laminate, vinyl, or tile, a lightweight cordless stick vacuum can be a practical choice for everyday cleaning. You don’t necessarily need an aggressive brush roll to clean hard floors, but you do want a floorhead that can pick up fine dust or large debris without scattering everything across the floor.

According to recent reports, some models, like the Dyson V15 Detect, have soft roller brushes that make close contact with hard floors, while others use multi-surface brush rolls that handle both hard floors and low-pile rugs. If your home has a combination of surfaces, look for a cordless stick vacuum with an automatic floor-detection feature that adjusts suction as you move between thresholds.

According to recent reports, cordless convenience is a big selling point. You can grab your vacuum for a quick kitchen cleanup without dragging out a full-size model or having to look for an accessible wall outlet. Just pay attention to battery life, dustbin capacity, and how much suction you get at the highest power mode. Runtime claims can be optimistic when using motorized attachments or boost settings.

Dyson V15 Detect Cordless Vacuum.

Bissell PowerClean FurFinder Cordless Stick Vacuum.

Tineco Pure ONE Station 5 Pro Cordless Vacuum.

Recent findings suggest that pet hair has its way of working itself into everything, especially carpet, upholstery, and rugs. If you’re constantly battling shedding, pick a vacuum with a motorized brush roll that lifts hair instead of just pushing it around. Tangle-resistant brush rolls, anti-hair-wrap technology, and specialized attachments make a noticeable difference when cleaning up after furry friends.

Sources indicate that both uprights and cordless stick vacuums are good choices here. A full-size upright, such as the Bissell CleanView Swivel Rewind offers the power and capacity for more demanding whole-home cleaning (without the hefty price tag, too). A pet-focused cordless stick like the Levoit LVAC-300 with specialized attachments helps tackle furniture and stairs.

Bissell CleanView Swivel Rewind Pet Upright Bagless Vacuum.

Bissell Pet Hair Eraser DualBrush Vacuum.

Dyson Ball Animal 3 Vacuum Cleaner.

Industry observers note that robot vacuums are ideal for keeping floors relatively tidy between more involved cleaning sessions. They work well for homes with mostly hard flooring where dust, crumbs, and everyday debris tend to accumulate swiftly. Many newer models also handle low- to medium-pile carpeting, automatically adjusting suction when they detect a different surface.

If you’re shopping for one, pay attention to navigation, obstacle avoidance, and the size of the dustbin. Self-emptying docks are a huge help if you don’t want to empty the vacuum after every run. Some models, like the Roborock Qrevo Series QV 35A, have mopping capabilities, taking care of two different chores with one home appliance.

According to recent reports, I wouldn’t necessarily recommend a robot as your only vacuum if you have thick carpet, pets, or lots of furniture and tight corners. Think of it as a maintenance tool that handles daily stuff while a traditional vacuum takes care of a more thorough cleaning.

Roborock Qrevo Series QV 35A Robot Vacuum and Mop.

Eureka J15 Pro Ultra Robot Vacuum and Mop.

Ecovacs Deebot X12 Omnicyclone Robot Vacuum and Mop.

Take stock of your flooring, how much space you need to clean, and the kinds of messes you deal with most often. A cordless stick vacuum might be all you need for a smaller home with hardwood floors, but a full-size upright is a better investment if you have mostly carpeted rooms and pets. If convenience is the priority, a robot keeps everyday debris under control.

And remember, you don’t necessarily need one machine to do it all. Sometimes the best setup is actually a combination. The right choice is ultimately the one that makes cleaning your floors a little less of a chore.

PortMiami closed fiscal year 2026 with nearly two million passengers more than in the previous year, setting a newly introduced record.

The port has shared that a record 10,533,854 cruise passengers, a 23 percent increase from the 8,564,225 during the previous fiscal year, visited during fiscal year 2026, which ran from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026.

As previously reported, the 10-million passenger milestone was achieved on September 14.

“Crossing the 10 million passenger threshold showcases the strength of our partnerships and the commitment of our team,” remarked the recently appointed port director and CEO Jonathan Daniels.

“As we enhance our facilities and streamline operations, PortMiami is well positioned to support the next era of growth in travel and trade.”.

The port added that the momentum is continuing in the first month of fiscal year 2027.

In October 2026, there were 832,142 cruise passengers across 106 cruise calls, the highest October total in the port’s history.

This represents a 19.04 and 13.98 percent increase compared to 699,043 passenger movements and 93 cruise calls in 2025, respectively.

According to recent reports, “These milestones reflect PortMiami’s continued momentum and the extraordinary work taking place across our seaport. Our investments in modern and resilient infrastructure are delivering results that strengthen our community and expand opportunities for residents and businesses alike,” stated Miami Dade County Mayor Daniella Levine Cava.

The ship was one of the seven named during a recent simultaneous ceremony in Amsterdam that virtually connected locations across Europe and Egypt.

“For nearly three decades, Viking has offered travelers a meaningful way to explore the history and culture of Europe through river travel,” remarked Leah Talactac, president and CEO of Viking.

“We are pleased to welcome the Viking Halogi to our award-winning fleet and to offer even more curious travelers the opportunity to experience Europe in Viking comfort.”.

Hosting 190 guests in 95 staterooms, the Viking Halogi will operate itineraries including the “Rhine Getaway” and “Christmas on the Rhine,” as well as the newly introduced “Oberammergau, Innsbruck & the Rhine” itinerary offered in 2030.

Like its sister ships, it features Scandinavian design and the asymmetric corridor layout that allows for true two-room suites.

As confirmed during a recent earnings call, Viking’s orderbook is growing.

The firm expects to take delivery of 25 additional river ships by 2030, 11 additional ocean ships by 2032 and two additional expedition ships by 2031.

This means that its fleet will comprise 123 river ships in 2030 and 28 ocean and expedition ships in 2032.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review.
  • Here’s what you’ll learn when you read this story:.
  • It has been revealed that scattered sparsely across Earth’s surface, from Nebraska to Mali to the Philippines, drilling rigs are rising from platforms surrounded by sheds and tanks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us?

Here’s what you’ll learn when you read this story:.

It has been revealed that scattered sparsely across Earth’s surface, from Nebraska to Mali to the Philippines, drilling rigs are rising from platforms surrounded by sheds and tanks. Each contains a tower 10 to 15 stories high. Only they aren’t pumping fossil fuels. While they’re reminiscent of machinery used to extract oil and gas, these rigs are on the hunt for a different type of gas—one trapped in microscopic pores of rock—that some researchers believe could help solve humanity’s clean energy needs for hundreds of years. Or at least offset our ever-increasing demand.

Natural stores of hydrogen gas exist throughout our planet’s crust on every continent. It’s colorless and odorless, and it frequently escapes into the atmosphere through natural seeps or during mining for metals like copper and zinc. But finding it in commercially viable quantities has always been difficult. Now, researchers and entrepreneurs think they have reason to hope this challenge can be overcome.

“There are definitely places where we’re going to find natural hydrogen accumulations, and in those places it’s going to be a very competitive energy source,” says Pete Johnson, CEO and cofounder of hydrogen exploration firm Koloma. The company plans to drill 20 wells in the next two years in some of “the best hydrogen systems” in the world, including in the U.S. and the Philippines.

It has been revealed that hydrogen is already a multibillion-dollar global industry. Fertilizer companies combine it with nitrogen to make ammonia. Oil refineries use it to lower the sulfur content in diesel. Metalworkers use it to prevent oxidation. Hydrogen is “an essential element for survival of humanity,” notes Ukrainian geochemist Viacheslav Zgonnik, PhD. But nearly all of the hydrogen used in those processes is manufactured, and much of it from methane gas in an energy-intensive way. So energy intensive, in fact, that companies produce 9 to 11 tons of carbon dioxide for every 1 ton of hydrogen, according to the Environmental and Energy Study Institute.

Some companies are exploring ways to produce hydrogen with fewer carbon emissions. But even so-called green hydrogen still requires energy to produce and may never be economically viable at scale, states Zgonnik. That’s where natural hydrogen deposits enter the picture. And scientists and prospectors believe natural hydrogen could serve far more industries than just fertilizer and petroleum production. Some even envision it could help power the world with near-zero carbon emissions in the process.

Exactly how much hydrogen exists, however, is still up for debate. A 2024 U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) paper modeled the amount of hydrogen likely to percolate under the surface and found enormous amounts. The bulk is likely “impractical to recover,” according to the paper published in Science Advances, but if even a small fraction of the total amount could be captured, it “would supply the projected hydrogen needed to reach net-zero emissions for [about] 200 years.”.

A 2025 report from The Royal Society was more cautious, tempering the optimism of the USGS model by using currently available hydrogen survey data. But even that suggested hydrogen “could be a game changer.”.

Hydrogen forms naturally through at least two processes: chemical reactions between water and iron-rich rocks, and the splitting of water molecules by radiation in rocks containing uranium, according to the Royal Society paper. The gas then saturates porous rock, akin to an underground sponge sealed on the top by a dense layer of caprock such as clay or other sedimentary rocks. Stick a straw—or in practical terms a drill—into the sponge, and out comes the hydrogen.

Known hydrogen accumulations occur in the oldest and most stable rocks on Earth at the core of the continents. Researchers speculate it exists in places where Earth’s crust tried to separate, like the Midcontinent Rift, which stretches beneath portions of Kansas, Iowa, Minnesota, and Wisconsin, and the Great Rift Valley in eastern Africa. The gas has also been found in regions where tectonic plates collided, including parts of the Pacific Rim off the coasts of North America and Asia, states Canadian hydrogen researcher Barbara Sherwood Lollar, PhD.

But natural underground hydrogen, also called gold or white hydrogen, has been discovered in plenty of other locations, too. In Mali, a country in western Africa, drillers searching for fresh water discovered a natural hydrogen system. Decades later, the Bourakebougou field, as it is called, began to produce enough hydrogen to supply electricity to a nearby village.

Local supplies of natural hydrogen could be among the gas’s first and most practical applications, notes Lollar, who has studied natural hydrogen for decades, one of the few early researchers investigating hydrogen as a potential source for clean energy. In May, she coauthored a paper in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences detailing how more than 70 percent of the continental crust “has the potential for hydrogen generation.” That widespread distribution, she says, could make the gas a source of local and regional power.

“Another one of the easy wins in all of this would be to use this hydrogen not just for a small community,” notes Sherwood Lollar, a University of Toronto professor. “The same rocks that produce hydrogen and helium are the rocks that produce nickel, copper, gold, diamonds, critical minerals.” That means mining conglomerates could capture hydrogen already being vented and use it to power their facilities.

According to recent reports, johnson takes the idea a step further. Industries that require large amounts of power, such as data centers, or industries that require hydrogen, like fertilizer manufacturers, could relocate to places where natural hydrogen is abundant, reducing the need to transport the gas.

Companies like Koloma are already surveying for economically viable deposits around the world. Johnson claims his organization has identified several potential fields.

Sources indicate that assuming the hydrogen reservoirs are large enough to economically produce, the process would look much like drilling for natural gas, he says. The timeline for developing the industry could be similar, too.

“We’re in some early innings right now,” Johnson says. “I mean if you look at how long it took us to develop the concept of shale gas, that was a 20- to 30-year process.”.

Then a few years after companies began drilling successful wells, the shale gas industry boomed. Natural hydrogen could follow a similar trajectory. Some companies are also exploring ways to stimulate hydrogen production underground by injecting heat and water into rocks before extracting the resulting gas. Those efforts, however, remain in their infancy.

Natural hydrogen could do more than help satisfy humanity’s insatiable appetite for energy—made worse by the buildout of energy-hungry data centers. It could also reshape the global energy map.

Industry observers note that “If the Philippines, for example, has domestic energy, what it means is that its neighboring countries like Taiwan, Japan, all these energy-poor countries may also have it,” Johnson says. “Anytime you find a newly introduced energy source in new places, it sort of rewrites the rules of geopolitics.”.

It has been revealed that he’s not certain exactly what role the gas will play in the world’s future energy portfolio. Will it render oil and gas obsolete, or will it become no more than a bit player? “That’s the question we’re trying to answer.”.

First, researchers and prospectors need to hunt down untapped hydrogen reservoirs and prove that they’re worth drilling.

Her work has appeared in National Geographic, Outdoor Life, The Atlantic, High Country News and Upcoming York Times, among others. She is also a 2025 Alicia Patterson Foundation fellow.
